title: analytics-replication-topology-adaptive-watermarking-and-redaction-playbook
creator: Maya Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Redwood Console telemetry and per-tenant usage records must be replicated across regions for query locality, redundancy, and analytics. Some tenants have strict residency requirements that disallow copying PII or certain fields out of their home region. Current replication is coarse-grained and cannot: 1) enforce field-level redaction at replication time, 2) coordinate durable eviction when residency policies conflict with regional failover, or 3) provide a predictable SLA for eventual materialization and backfills.

Objective: Build a replication orchestrator and execution playbook that provides: adaptive watermarking for per-tenant replication progress, field-level redaction hooks evaluated at source or proxy-write time, a soft-eviction/tombstone-escrow mechanism for safe regional quarantine, and an operator-friendly policy UI and audit trail in the Console. This must support near-real-time analytics use cases (1-10s fanout latency target) while preserving cost and SLO constraints.

High-level design:
- Topology: introduce a per-tenant replication manifest (lightweight protobuf) that lists allowed target regions, redaction rules (field names, redaction mode), and retention windows. The manifest is signed and stored in the control plane; runtime workers consult it before emitting change events.
- Adaptive watermarking: each tenant-stream maintains a logical watermark vector (source-log-offset, last-acked-region-offsets). Watermarks drive minimal re-replication windows and backfill candidates.
- Redaction hooks: two evaluation points: (A) source-side redact before encryption-and-publish for tenants with strict policies; (B) proxy-side redact at regional ingress for tenants that allow regional copies but require pseudonymization. Hooks are pluggable to support KMS/HSM and deterministic tokenization.
- Soft-eviction with tombstone escrow: when a tenant changes residency to restrict a target region, the orchestrator issues an eviction intent. Events already replicated are not immediately deleted; they are marked tombstone-escrow and quarantined for a remediation window (configurable, default 72h). During the window, rollbacks or legal holds can be applied; after the window, a scrubbing pipeline safely deletes encrypted payloads and emits an audit record.
- Consistency and SLOs: define per-tenant replication SLOs (p99 replication lag <= 10s for hot tenants, p99 durability 24h) and budgeted cost tiers. Replica fallback: if a preferred region is unavailable, automatic failover to compatible region variants occurs only if manifest allows it; otherwise, requests are queued with a backpressure signal to the Console API.

Acceptance criteria:
- New manifest schema v1 is stored and versioned in control plane; Console exposes editor with validation.
- Replication workers enforce redaction hooks for 100% of writes for tenants with redaction-enabled flag.
- Eviction flow completes full tombstone lifecycle (intent -> quarantine -> scrub -> audit log) in a test harness.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating failover behavior and SLO adherence for a sample of 20 tenants across 3 regions.
- Dashboards: per-tenant watermark lag, quarantine queue size, scrub throughput, and failed-redaction rates.

Operational runbook (short):
1) On manifest update, orchestration publishes a manifest-change event and triggers a manifest rollout job.
2) If a mismatch (worker hasn't applied redaction rules), circuit-break replication for the tenant and escalate.
3) Eviction scenario: set state to EVICTION_PENDING, notify SOC, start quarantine cron, and capture snapshot for legal review.
4) Post-scrub: emit signed audit entry and increment tenant-version pointer.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Source-side redaction increases CPU and latency at write time but provides the strongest privacy guarantee. We allow hybrid proxy redaction for cost-sensitive tenants.
- Tombstone escrow increases storage briefly but avoids irreversible data loss and supports legal holds. Default quarantine window balances compliance and storage cost.
- Watermark vectors increase control-plane metadata size; we shard by tenant groups and compact stale vectors periodically.

Implementation milestones:
- Phase 1 (MVP, 3 sprints): manifest schema + Console editor, worker checkpoint hooks, basic watermark propagation, and unit test harness.
- Phase 2 (3 sprints): redaction plugin infrastructure, tombstone-escrow implementation, end-to-end replication tests, and monitoring.
- Phase 3 (2 sprints): operator runbook automation, canary rollout for 50 tenants, cost analysis, and GA docs.

Security/privacy notes: integrate with KMS for tokenization keys; all audit logs must be append-only and signed. Formal security review required before Phase 2 rollout.

Open questions:
- Legal hold integration: should escrowed tombstones remain encrypted under customer KMS or Redwood KMS? (security/legal input needed)
- Quarantine default window: 72h vs 7d trade-off needs CX/Legal alignment.
- Backpressure semantics for Console API when replication targets are restricted: return 429 vs 202 with delayed consistency?

comments: 2025-11-06 - Kickoff: aligned on goals with PMs (Sofia Martinez) and Legal (Hannah O'Neil). Created initial proto shape and sketch of watermark vector. Action: prototype worker hook.

2025-11-20 - Prototype results: source-side redaction adds ~6ms median to write-path in our microbench; acceptable for non-latency-critical routes. Liam suggested offloading heavy tokenization to async workers for the lowest-latency customers.
2025-12-10 - Design review: PMs requested operator controls in Console for quarantine window and scrub scheduling. UX task created (DES-2143).
2026-01-15 - Security sync: KMS-integration approved in principle; Legal prefers escrow encrypted under customer KMS when available. Added dependency: KMS key rotation handling in scrub job.
2026-02-02 - PR #142 opened with manifest proto and basic worker gating. CI flaky on Windows-based tests; retriggered.
2026-02-18 - Perf tests: watermark metadata compaction reduced control-plane DB growth by 35% in our synthetic workload. Need to validate under 5k tenants per region.
2026-03-03 - Canary kickoff: selecting 8 internal tenants and 12 low-risk customers for initial rollout. Notified Support and CS. Metrics tracked: replication-lag, quarantine-size, scrub-error-rate.
2026-03-09 - Code review feedback from infra team (PR#142): add idempotency marker on eviction intent and improve instrumentation for scrubs. Liam addressing in PR#142-2.
2026-03-10 - Blocker discovered: cross-region KMS access patterns increase IAM policy complexity. Raised as dependency for cloud infra and created ticket ENG-118799.
Operational notes: include playbook snippet for SOC to suspend replication for a tenant quickly: set manifest 'replicate:false' and run 'orchestrator pause-tenant <tenant>' command.
